docs.text: Unidentified floating objects seen off the coast of Chicago. (Presumably vessels, distorted by the “Fata Morgana effect” during the frigid weather this morning on Lake Michigan.)

A late 18th-century Anishinaabe bag from the Great Lakes, featuring finger-woven images of the important supernatural beings Underwater Panther on one side and Thunderbird on the other; this bag would have held a medicine bundle.

Man’s Shoulder Bag Date: c. 1875–1900
Artist: Winnebago (Ho-Chunk/Native American) Western Great Lakes, northeastern Woodlands
I remade this using an image from my textbook. A beaded bag from an Indigenous Tribe near the Great Lakes
A Great Lakes Indigenous bag drawn in London in 1780 by Sarah Stone with a thunderbird design; it was on display at the Leverian Museum. Again the metal trade jingles give voice to the thunderbirds.
who painted this excellent painting of the Battle of Lake Erie?
Weird optical illusion of this thing looking to be floating above the horizon. It's moved a lot in the moments since I took the photo, so pretty sure it's a ship headed to Harbourfront. #LakeOntario

10/2:40 a.m. A Coast Guard vessel in Lake Superior among the Apostle Islands, Wisconsin, sees a large, yellow- white, oblong object that appears and reappears briefly in a slightly different position each time. [Eberhart]

Small Giants by Brazilian artist Alex Senna was located at Wendy Park, The sculptures are positioned uniquely: the boy looks out towards the city, and the girl gazes at Lake Erie, symbolizing a connection between urban life and natural beauty.

A FATA MORGANA IN OHIO: "Last Thursday morning at Edgewater Beach, Ohio, photographer Tyler Penland witnessed something strange on the Lake Erie horizon. A massive tanker ship appeared to hover above the water—its form stretched and distorted, as if suspended in midair..." Spaceweather.com
